$description: Bonbibi design tokens. Three tiers: primitive (raw values), semantic (aliases only), component (until a second component needs it). DTCG dimension units are restricted to px and rem, so viewport-relative sizing is not expressible here.

primitive.$description: Raw values only. Nothing in this tier carries meaning.

bengali.$description: Keeps 8 ink parts at 24 px against Noto's 7, so one more conjunct survives a 1-bit threshold.

malayalam.$description: Shortest ink box of the candidates at 23 px, and carries the chillu-n + virama + rra reading of nta.

script.$description: Per-script floor and leading. A script with three vertical zones needs more pixels per glyph AND more rows per line; only the first of those is a font size. Ink boxes measured from 1-bit rasters at 24 px.

px-per-mm-inline.$description: 800 px across the 154.08 mm active width of the Raspberry Pi Touch Display.

px-per-mm-block.$description: 480 px across the 85.92 mm active height. The block axis is binding: it carries more pixels per millimetre, so a given pixel count is physically smaller there and fails the 9.6 mm minimum first.

pixel-aspect.$description: Dot pitch is 0.1926 mm inline against 0.1790 mm block (0.0642 mm per subpixel, RGB stripe). Pixels are 7.6% wider than they are tall. Multiply an inline dimension by this to get the block dimension that renders physically square. Set to 1 on square-pixel targets.

semantic.$description: Aliases only. Zero literal values, so the graph is walkable. STATUS and DEPTH are formally separate layers; no token appears in both, and the separation is machine-checked.

status.$description: Layer A. The only layer permitted to express a safety judgement. Every colour is paired with a mandatory shape.

$extensions.bonbibi.meaning: mandatory action; the primary control and nothing else
outside the terrain or street-graph extent

depth.$description: Layer B. Informational measurement of water depth in metres. May never, alone, carry a verdict. No hazard level is ever encoded in blue (ISO 22324:2022 clause 4.3.3).

$extensions.bonbibi.note: Supplementary fatal-danger indication only. Must co-occur with the red danger status marker and the text label. Does not replace red.

casing-low.$description: Band-boundary casing below D3. Asserted at 3:1 or better against both adjacent fills.

casing-high.$description: Band-boundary casing at and above D3.

size.$description: Target sizes are per-axis because the panel's pixels are not square. A 52 px square measures 10.02 mm inline and 9.31 mm block, which passes on one axis and fails on the other.

target-min-inline.$description: 9.63 mm. Parhi et al.: >= 9.2 mm single-target, >= 9.6 mm multi-target.

target-primary-inline.$description: 12.33 mm. Headroom for wet hands and stress tremor.

target-gap.$description: 2.31 mm inline, 2.15 mm block. Clears the 2 mm minimum on both axes.

body-min-latin.$description: Latin and Portuguese only. Measured ink box 19 px; holds 19 parts unchanged from 16 px to 40 px, so 20 px is comfortably above its threshold.

body-min-bengali.$description: 24 px. At 16 px three conjuncts weld shut under a 1-bit threshold (5 ink parts against 8 at 40 px).

body-min-malayalam.$description: 24 px. Reaches full part separation here; one region is welded at 16 and 20 px.

body-min-nastaliq.$description: 24 px. Nastaliq does not weld — it reaches 16 of 16 parts here. Its cost is rows, not legibility.

leading-malayalam.$description: PROPOSED. No panel carries a Malayalam locale yet.

leading-nastaliq.$description: PROPOSED. No panel carries an Urdu or Sindhi locale yet.

body-min.$description: DEPRECATED as a global floor: there is no single body minimum. Aliases the Latin floor for compatibility; per-script consumers must use body-min-<script>. Original note: A font size is a block-axis quantity, so it divides by 5.5866 alone. 18 px on this panel is only 3.22 mm.

chrome.$description: 3.58 mm. Chrome labels, set in Jersey 20 — one whole cell.

readout.$description: 8.95 mm. Two whole Jersey 25 cells. Replaces 48 px, which was not cell-aligned.

hero.$description: 17.90 mm. Four whole Jersey 25 cells. Replaces 78 px: the brief asked for at least 13.8 mm and 75 px would give only 13.43 mm, so the next whole multiple of the cell is the smallest size that satisfies both the physical minimum and the grid.

cell-alignment.$description: Jersey 20 has a 20 px design grid and Jersey 25 a 25 px grid, so a bitmap face is only crisp at whole multiples: 20/40 and 25/50/75/100. Noto Sans has no cell, so body prose is bound only by the 20 px physical floor. ONE stated exception: the five depth-band letters inside the gauge are 16 px, because a 20 px glyph does not fit a 25 px band — they are redundant labelling, and the hazard legend carries the same names at 20 px.

rendering.$description: Never subpixel. The RGB stripe would buy horizontal resolution by laying a coloured fringe on every stem, on a device where colour is reserved for signal. Keep the fonts' TrueType hinting instructions; subset glyph coverage if you must, never the instructions.

integer-only.$description: Every dimension in the system is an integer px so that x2 (1600 x 960) and x3 (2400 x 1440) are exact. 1920 x 1080 is not an integer multiple of 800 x 480; the desktop view renders the x2 canvas centred and letterboxed, never a reflow.

family-computed.$description: Depths, distances, counts, times, coordinates. Jersey 25 is proportional, so the readout component routes every figure through a fixed cell as wide as the widest digit rather than relying on tabular-nums.

family-composed.$description: The language model's narration. Never used for a computed value.

component.$description: A token stays here until a second component needs it, at which point it is promoted to semantic.

scale-max-m.$description: The scale breaks above 1.20 m rather than compressing D4.

tick-major-m.$description: Numerals appear only on this level. Rank is encoded by tick length, never by colour.

stroke.$description: In viewBox units. Renders at 2 px at the 24 px minimum size.

riser-max.$description: Riser heights are limit / max(limit) * riser-max. 0.10 -> 20%, 0.30 -> 60%, 0.50 -> 100%. Generated from the same constant as the gauge notch offsets; a test asserts they agree.
